books.section: Topic 1.3 European exploration in the Americas
The Early Colonial Era: Spain Colonizes the New World

options.text: Spain had promised Portugal military support against France in exchange for the American lands
options.misconception: No such bargain existed; the treaty was a papal division, not a military deal.

options.text: Portugal believed the Americas held no wealth worth claiming and preferred to focus on Africa
options.misconception: Portugal did claim American land; the line gave it Brazil, which it kept.

options.text: Portugal's king had agreed to abandon all claims in the Americas in exchange for African gold
options.misconception: Portugal never abandoned its American claims; the line gave it Brazil.

options.text: The line protected Portugal's African sea route to Asia and secured Brazil for Portugal

rationales.general:
1. Ask what Portugal wanted most. Its ships were rounding Africa toward the spice trade of Asia.
2. Ask what the line gave Portugal. Everything east of it, including the African coast route and Brazil.
3. Ask what Portugal gave up. Lands west of the line, which it had not explored and did not yet value.
4. Check the trade. Portugal kept its route and gained Brazil, so the line was a win, not a loss.
Remember: judge a bargain by what each side valued most, not by how much land each side got.
rationales.D: Portugal cared most about the sea route to Asia around Africa, and the line kept Spain out of that route. Brazil came with the line's eastern side, so Portugal kept both its route and an American claim.
rationales.A: The treaty was settled by papal mediation between the two crowns, not by a promise of military help. No record of such a bargain exists.
rationales.B: Portugal valued Brazil enough to keep it, and the line gave it to Portugal. A crown does not accept a line that gives away land it wants.
rationales.C: The treaty gave Portugal Brazil, so Portugal kept an American claim rather than abandoning one. Abandoning the Americas was never part of the deal.

stem: The Treaty of Tordesillas drew its dividing line 370 leagues west of the Cape Verde islands, giving Portugal Brazil and Spain the rest of the Americas. Which of the following best explains why Portugal accepted a line that gave Spain most of the Americas?

stimulus.source_note: Paraphrase of the Treaty of Tordesillas (1494); the 370-league line west of the Cape Verde islands is the treaty's term.
stimulus.text: The 1494 agreement, brokered with the pope's approval, divided all newly discovered lands between the two Iberian crowns along a meridian 370 leagues west of the Cape Verde islands.
